question:
I which year, did Sher Khan defeat Humayun at Kanauj?

[SSC MTS ]
options: 1541
1543
1540
1542
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1540

Explanation:
Sher Khan (later known as Sher Shah Suri) defeated Humayun in the Battle of Kannauj (Battle of Bilgram) in 1540 CE. This battle was a decisive conflict between the Mughal Empire and the Sur Empire. Sher Khan showcased his military strategy and organizational skills, forcing Humayun to flee India and seek refuge in Persia. After this victory, Sher Shah Suri captured Delhi and established the Sur Empire.

Extra Facts:
Sher Shah Suri introduced significant administrative and military reforms during his reign (1540-1545), including the rupee and paisa currency system, construction of the Grand Trunk Road, and land revenue reforms. His policies later influenced Akbar's rule.

Explanation:
शेर खान (जिसे बाद में शेर शाह सूरी के नाम से जाना गया) ने 1540 ईस्वी में कन्नौज के युद्ध (बिलग्राम का युद्ध) में हुमायूँ को हराया था। यह युद्ध मुगल साम्राज्य और सूरी साम्राज्य के बीच एक निर्णायक संघर्ष था। शेर खान ने अपनी सैन्य रणनीति और संगठन कौशल का प्रदर्शन करते हुए हुमायूँ को पराजित किया, जिसके बाद हुमायूँ को भारत छोड़कर फारस भागना पड़ा। इस युद्ध के बाद शेर शाह सूरी ने दिल्ली पर कब्जा कर लिया और सूरी साम्राज्य की स्थापना की।

Extra Facts:
शेर शाह सूरी ने अपने शासनकाल (1540-1545) में कई प्रशासनिक और सैन्य सुधार किए, जिनमें रुपया और पैसा की मुद्रा प्रणाली, ग्रैंड ट्रंक रोड का निर्माण, और भू-राजस्व प्रणाली में सुधार शामिल हैं। उनकी नीतियों का प्रभाव बाद में अकबर के शासन में भी देखा गया।

question:
Who among the following was the successor of Mughal Emperor, Babur?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Shahjahan
Humayun
Jahangir
Aurangzeb
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Humayun

Explanation:
Humayun was the successor of the Mughal Emperor Babur. Babur founded the Mughal Empire in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526. After Babur's death in 1530, his son Humayun ascended the throne. Humayun faced defeat against Sher Shah Suri in 1540 and spent 15 years in exile but regained Delhi in 1555 with Persian support. After his death, his son Akbar became the next Mughal ruler.

Extra Facts:
Babur wrote his autobiography, "Baburnama", in the Chagatai Turkic language, which is a crucial historical source. Humayun's reign was unstable, but he played a key role in preserving the Mughal Empire. He died in 1556 after falling from the stairs of his library.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन मुगल सम्राट बाबर का उत्तराधिकारी था?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options_hi: शाहजहाँ
हुमायूं
जहांगीर
औरंगज़ेब
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है हुमायूं

Explanation:
हुमायूं मुगल सम्राट बाबर का उत्तराधिकारी था। बाबर ने 1526 में पानीपत की पहली लड़ाई में इब्राहिम लोदी को हराकर भारत में मुगल साम्राज्य की स्थापना की। 1530 में बाबर की मृत्यु के बाद, उसका बेटा हुमायूं सिंहासन पर बैठा। हुमायूं ने 1540 में शेरशाह सूरी से हार के बाद 15 वर्षों तक निर्वासन में बिताया, लेकिन 1555 में फारसी सहायता से दिल्ली पर पुनः कब्जा किया। उसकी मृत्यु के बाद उसका पुत्र अकबर मुगल साम्राज्य का शासक बना।

Extra Facts:
बाबर ने अपनी आत्मकथा "बाबरनामा" तुर्की भाषा में लिखी, जो मुगल इतिहास का एक महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत है। हुमायूं का शासनकाल अस्थिर रहा, लेकिन उसने मुगल साम्राज्य को बचाए रखने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। उसकी मृत्यु 1556 में पुस्तकालय की सीढ़ियों से गिरने के कारण हुई।

question:
Which of the following was NOT commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: Jama Masjid, Delhi
Red Fort, Delhi
Humayun's Tomb, Delhi
Shahjahanabad, Delhi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Humayun's Tomb, Delhi

Explanation:
Emperor Shah Jahan (1628-1658 CE) commissioned several iconic structures during the golden age of Mughal architecture, including the Jama Masjid (Delhi), Red Fort (Delhi), and Shahjahanabad (the seventh city of Delhi). However, Humayun's Tomb was built much earlier (1565-1572 CE) by Humayun's widow, Hamida Banu Begum, before Shah Jahan's reign. Designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, it is India's first charbagh-style tomb and influenced the design of the Taj Mahal.

Extra Facts:
Shah Jahan is called the "Prince of Builders." He constructed the Taj Mahal (Agra) in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, considered the pinnacle of Mughal architecture. His reign is termed the "Golden Age" of the Mughal Empire, marked by advancements in art, culture, and architecture.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सम्राट शाहजहाँ द्वारा नहीं बनवाया गया था?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options_hi: जामा मस्जिद, दिल्ली
लाल किला, दिल्ली
हुमायूं का मकबरा, दिल्ली
शाहजहानाबाद, दिल्ली
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है हुमायूं का मकबरा, दिल्ली

Explanation:
सम्राट शाहजहाँ (1628-1658 ई.) ने मुगल वास्तुकला के स्वर्ण युग में कई प्रसिद्ध इमारतों का निर्माण करवाया, जिनमें जामा मस्जिद (दिल्ली), लाल किला (दिल्ली), और शाहजहानाबाद (दिल्ली का सातवाँ शहर) शामिल हैं। हालाँकि, हुमायूं का मकबरा का निर्माण 1565-1572 ई. में शाहजहाँ के शासनकाल से पहले ही हुमायूं की पत्नी हमीदा बानो बेगम द्वारा करवाया गया था। इसका डिज़ाइन फारसी वास्तुकार मिराक मिर्ज़ा गियास ने तैयार किया था और यह भारत में प्रथम चारबाग शैली वाला मकबरा है, जिसने ताजमहल के डिज़ाइन को प्रभावित किया।

Extra Facts:
शाहजहाँ को "इमारतों का राजकुमार" कहा जाता है। उसने ताजमहल (आगरा) को अपनी पत्नी मुमताज़ महल की याद में बनवाया, जो मुगल वास्तुकला का शिखर माना जाता है। उसके शासनकाल को मुगल साम्राज्य का "स्वर्ण युग" कहा जाता है, जहाँ कला, संस्कृति और वास्तुकला का विशेष विकास हुआ।

question:
Name the French jeweler who traveled to India at least six times during the Mughal period.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Antonio Monserrate
Jean-Baptiste Tavernier
Seydi Ali Reis
Peter Mundy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jean-Baptiste Tavernier

Explanation:
Jean-Baptiste Tavernier was a French jeweler and traveler who visited India six times during the Mughal Empire in the 17th century. He explored various parts of India, particularly cities like Golconda and Agra, where he traded diamonds and other precious gems. His book, 'The Six Voyages of Jean-Baptiste Tavernier', provides crucial insights into the economic, social, and cultural aspects of Mughal India. He also mentioned the Koh-i-Noor diamond, which later became part of the British Crown Jewels.

Extra Facts:
Tavernier’s travel accounts highlight trade, mining, and royal lifestyles during the Mughal era. He witnessed the reigns of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb and participated in their courts. His reports reveal the significance of the diamond trade in the Mughal Empire. He also documented relations between European traders and Indian rulers.

Explanation:
जीन बेप्टिस्ट टैवर्नियर एक फ्रांसीसी जौहरी और यात्री थे, जिन्होंने 17वीं शताब्दी में मुगल साम्राज्य के दौरान भारत की छः बार यात्रा की। उन्होंने अपनी यात्राओं के दौरान भारत के विभिन्न हिस्सों, विशेषकर गोलकुंडा और आगरा जैसे शहरों का दौरा किया, जहाँ उन्होंने हीरों और अन्य बहुमूल्य रत्नों का व्यापार किया। उनकी पुस्तक 'द सिक्स वोयाजेस ऑफ जीन-बैप्टिस्ट टैवर्नियर' मुगल भारत के आर्थिक, सामाजिक और सांस्कृतिक पहलुओं पर महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी प्रदान करती है। उन्होंने कोहिनूर हीरे का भी उल्लेख किया, जो बाद में ब्रिटिश राजशाही का हिस्सा बना।

Extra Facts:
टैवर्नियर के यात्रा वृत्तांत मुगल काल के व्यापार, खनन और शाही जीवनशैली पर प्रकाश डालते हैं। उन्होंने शाहजहाँ और औरंगजेब के शासनकाल को देखा और उनके दरबारों में भाग लिया। उनकी रिपोर्ट्स से पता चलता है कि मुगल साम्राज्य में हीरों का व्यापार कितना महत्वपूर्ण था। उन्होंने यूरोपीय व्यापारियों और भारतीय शासकों के बीच संबंधों को भी दर्ज किया।

question:
Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal Empire during the period of _________.

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: 1657-1709
1656-1708
1658-1707
1655-1709
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1658-1707

Explanation:
Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal Empire from 1658 to 1707. He was the sixth Mughal emperor and came to power after deposing his father, Shah Jahan. His reign is known for both the territorial expansion of the empire and his religious orthodoxy. He reimposed the Jizya tax on non-Muslims and destroyed several Hindu temples. He died in 1707, after which the decline of the Mughal Empire began.

Extra Facts:
Aurangzeb was given the title 'Alamgir'. He fought prolonged wars against the Marathas in the Deccan, which weakened the Mughal Empire economically and militarily. He compiled the Fatawa-e-Alamgiri, a collection of Islamic laws.

question:
Who was the last Mughal emperor of India?

Explanation:
Bahadur Shah II was the last Mughal emperor of India, also known as 'Zafar'. His reign lasted from 1837 to 1857. During the First War of Indian Independence (1857), he led the rebels but was later arrested by the British and exiled to Rangoon (present-day Yangon), where he died in 1862. His exile marked the formal end of the Mughal Empire, as the British abolished the Mughal rule officially.

Extra Facts:
Bahadur Shah II was also a poet and Sufi thinker, composing verses in Urdu and Persian. His role in the 1857 revolt made him a symbol of India's freedom struggle. The British executed his sons and formally dissolved the Mughal Empire after his exile.

question:
The real name of Babur, the founder of Mughal dynasty in India was:

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Zahiruddin Muhammad
Irfanuddin Muhammad
Zainuddin Muhammad
Ruknuddin Muhammad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Zahiruddin Muhammad

Explanation:
Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, was originally named Zahiruddin Muhammad. He was born on 14 February 1483 in Fergana (present-day Uzbekistan). He was a descendant of both Timur and Genghis Khan. In 1526, he defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat, laying the foundation of the Mughal Empire. He wrote his autobiography, 'Baburnama', in Chagatai Turkic, which is a crucial source of Mughal history.

Extra Facts:
Babur was not only a skilled military leader but also a talented poet and writer. He introduced Mughal architecture in India, which was later developed by Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan. He died on 26 December 1530 in Agra and was buried in Kabul.

Extra Facts:

question:
The Din-i-Ilahi (lit. “Religion of God”) was syncretic religion propounded by:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Babur
Jahangir
Aurangzeb
Akbar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
Din-i-Ilahi was a syncretic religion propounded by Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1582 CE. It combined elements from Islam, Hinduism, Christianity, Jainism, and Zoroastrianism. Akbar aimed to promote religious harmony among his diverse subjects. However, this faith did not gain widespread acceptance and faded after his death. It was part of Akbar's policy of 'Sulh-e-Kul' (Universal Peace), emphasizing tolerance.

Extra Facts:
Akbar established the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) for interfaith discussions. He abolished the Jizya tax and promoted Hindu-Muslim unity. Prominent Hindu nobles like Birbal and Raja Todar Mal held key positions in his administration.

Explanation:
मुगल बादशाह बाबर नक्शबंदी सूफी सिलसिला का अनुयायी था। यह सिलसिला मध्य एशिया में उत्पन्न हुआ और इसका प्रभाव तैमूर और मुगल शासकों पर था। नक्शबंदी सूफियों ने शरीयत (इस्लामी कानून) के पालन पर जोर दिया और राजनीतिक मामलों में भी सक्रिय भूमिका निभाई। बाबर ने अपनी आत्मकथा 'बाबरनामा' में इस सिलसिले के प्रति अपनी श्रद्धा का उल्लेख किया है।

question:
The Taj Mahal was built by:

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: Humayun
Jahangir
Akbar
Shah Jahan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shah Jahan

Explanation:
The Taj Mahal was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. Constructed between 1632 and 1653, it was designed by renowned architects like Ustad Ahmad Lahori. The Taj Mahal is considered the finest example of Mughal architecture and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Made of white marble, its design blends Persian, Islamic, and Indian styles.

Extra Facts:
Shah Jahan commissioned several other significant structures during his reign (1628-1658), including the Red Fort and Jama Masjid. The Taj Mahal is regarded as a symbol of love and is one of the Seven Wonders of the World. Shah Jahan was later imprisoned by his son Aurangzeb, spending his final years gazing at the Taj Mahal from the Agra Fort.

Explanation:
ताजमहल का निर्माण मुग़ल बादशाह शाहजहां ने अपनी पत्नी मुमताज़ महल की याद में करवाया था। यह निर्माण 1632 से 1653 के बीच हुआ और इसे उस्ताद अहमद लाहौरी जैसे प्रसिद्ध वास्तुकारों ने डिज़ाइन किया था। ताजमहल को मुग़ल वास्तुकला का सर्वोत्कृष्ट उदाहरण माना जाता है और यह यूनेस्को की विश्व धरोहर सूची में शामिल है। यह सफेद संगमरमर से बना है और इसकी डिज़ाइन में फ़ारसी, इस्लामिक और भारतीय शैलियों का मिश्रण है।

question:
By which name was the Head of the Panchayat or the Village Headman called in Mughal India?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options: Samant
Mahant
Muqaddam
Khoran
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Muqaddam

Explanation:
In Mughal India, the Panchayat was the basic unit of rural administration, and its head was called the Muqaddam. This individual played a crucial role in village affairs, tax collection, and dispute resolution. The Muqaddam was elected by the villagers and acted as a link between local governance and revenue officials. The Mughal Empire encouraged the Panchayat system to maintain village autonomy while ensuring smooth revenue collection.

Extra Facts:
Other key figures in Mughal rural administration included the Patwari (accountant) and Chaudhary (tax collector). The Zamindars were also influential, acting as intermediaries between peasants and the empire. The Mughals relied on a decentralized system where village heads and local elites helped maintain order and revenue flow.

question:
Who made the use of Gunpowder common in North India to defeat enemies?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Ibrahim Lodi
Babur
Rana Sanga
Daulat Khan Lodi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Babur

Explanation:
Babur popularized the use of gunpowder in North India. He was the founder of the Mughal Empire and effectively used gunpowder and artillery to defeat Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526). This marked a significant turning point in Indian history as it revolutionized warfare tactics. Babur also employed the 'Tulguhma' and 'Rumi' strategies, which involved using cannons as mobile units on the battlefield.

Extra Facts:
Babur documented his Indian campaigns in his autobiography, 'Baburnama'. He not only introduced advanced military techniques but also patronized art and culture. His reign laid the foundation for Mughal architecture in India. The victory at Panipat established Mughal rule in India.

question:
Who was the Iranian ruler who attacked the city of Delhi and took away an immense amount of wealth in 1739 ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Ahmad Shah Qajar
Nadir shah
Ahmad Shah Abdali
Abbas |
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nadir Shah

Explanation:
Nadir Shah was a powerful Iranian ruler who invaded India in 1739 and plundered Delhi. He defeated the Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah Rangila in the Battle of Karnal (1739). Nadir Shah caused massive destruction in Delhi and looted precious treasures from the Mughals, including the 'Koh-i-Noor Diamond' and the 'Peacock Throne'. This attack severely weakened the Mughal Empire and paved the way for further foreign invasions in India.

Extra Facts:
Nadir Shah is also called the 'Napoleon of Persia'. He established his empire in Iran after the fall of the Safavid dynasty. His army committed brutal massacres in Delhi, similar to the 'Jallianwala Bagh massacre', killing thousands of civilians. After this plunder, the Mughal Empire's economy collapsed, leading to its eventual decline.

Among Babur's four sons, Humayun was the eldest. He was born in 1508 and succeeded Babur as the Mughal emperor in 1530 after his father's death. Humayun played a crucial role in establishing the Mughal Empire in India, though his reign was turbulent, marked by his defeat at the hands of Sher Shah Suri. Extra Facts:
बाबर ने 1526 में पानीपत की पहली लड़ाई में इब्राहिम लोदी को हराकर मुग़ल साम्राज्य की नींव रखी। उन्होंने आगरा को अपनी राजधानी बनाया और यहीं पर उनकी मृत्यु हुई। बाबर के बेटे हुमायूँ ने बाद में उनके शव को काबुल ले जाकर दफनाया, जहाँ आज बाबर की कब्र एक प्रसिद्ध पर्यटन स्थल है।

question:
Which of the following cities was built by Humayun at Delhi?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Akbarabad
Dinpanah
Muhammadabad
Siri
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dinpanah

Explanation:
Mughal Emperor Humayun founded the city of Dinpanah in Delhi in 1533 CE. It was one of his significant achievements during his reign. Dinpanah means 'Refuge of Faith'. Humayun developed it as his capital, but Sher Shah Suri defeated him in 1540 CE, destroyed the city, and shifted his capital to Sasaram. Later, Humayun recaptured Delhi in 1555 CE but could not revive Dinpanah.

Extra Facts:
Humayun's reign (1530-1540, 1555-1556) was turbulent for the Mughal Empire. He faced defeat against Sher Shah Suri but later regained Delhi with the help of the Persian Shah. Humayun died in 1556 CE after falling from the stairs of the Dinpanah Library.

question:
When did Akbar became the emperor?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1560 AD

1552 AD
1556 AD
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1556 AD

Explanation:
Akbar became the Mughal emperor on 14th February 1556 after the death of his father, Humayun. At that time, Akbar was only 13 years old, and his regent Bairam Khan assisted him in governance. Akbar's reign is considered the golden age of the Mughal Empire, marked by religious tolerance, administrative reforms, and patronage of art and culture.

Extra Facts:
Akbar consolidated his power by defeating Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556). He introduced Din-i-Ilahi, a syncretic religion blending elements of various faiths. Key reforms under Akbar included the Mansabdari system and the abolition of the Jizya tax.

question:
The office of Diwan-i-Insha dealt with which affair in administration?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Military
Religious affairs
Finance
State correspondence
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State correspondence

Explanation:
The Diwan-i-Insha was an important department in the Mughal administration that dealt with state correspondence. This department was responsible for drafting and maintaining royal decrees (firmans), letters, proclamations, and other official documents. Its head was called the Dabir-i-Khas, who was responsible for composing letters in the royal language and style. This department played a crucial role in facilitating smooth communication between the Sultan, governors, and other officials, ensuring the centralized administration of the Mughal Empire.

Extra Facts:
Other key departments in Mughal administration included Diwan-i-Arz (Military), Diwan-i-Wazarat (Finance), and Diwan-i-Risalat (Religious affairs). The Diwan-i-Insha also helped in preserving royal records and authenticating state messages.

question:
What were cash crops such as cotton and sugarcane called during the Mughal period?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options: Jins-i-kamil
Jins-i-shukr
Jins-i-tagh
Jins-i-qiblis
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jins-i-kamil

Explanation:
During the Mughal period, cash crops such as cotton and sugarcane were referred to as 'Jins-i-kamil', an Arabic term meaning 'superior crops'. Agriculture was a vital part of the Mughal economy, and cash crops held special significance as they were major sources of trade and revenue. Under Akbar's reign, agricultural reforms were emphasized, and Todar Mal streamlined the land revenue system (known as the 'Zabti System').

Extra Facts:
Mughal agriculture was categorized into two main seasons: Rabi (winter crops) and Kharif (monsoon crops). Cash crops generated substantial revenue for the empire, which was used for military and administrative expenses. Both Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb saw further growth in agricultural production.

मुगल काल में कपास और गन्ना जैसी नकदी फसलों को 'जिन्स-ए-कामिल' कहा जाता था। यह शब्द अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है 'उत्तम फसलें'। मुगल साम्राज्य में कृषि अर्थव्यवस्था का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा थी, और नकदी फसलों को विशेष महत्व दिया जाता था क्योंकि ये व्यापार और राजस्व का प्रमुख स्रोत थीं। अकबर के शासनकाल में कृषि सुधारों पर विशेष ध्यान दिया गया था, और टोडरमल ने भू-राजस्व प्रणाली (जिसे 'जब्ती प्रणाली' कहा जाता था) को सुव्यवस्थित किया था।
